note: Frozen labeled corpus for the #504 citation-support shadow gate.

pairs.rationale: The passage restates the claim word for word, so the citation fully supports it.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone led the Vellum Robotics platform team through the 2024 migration to a new event bus.
pairs.passage: Avery Stone led the Vellum Robotics platform team through the 2024 migration to a new event bus.

pairs.rationale: Every element of the claim (name, employer, title, year) appears verbatim in the passage.
pairs.claimStatement: In 2025, Blake Harbour worked as a senior staff engineer at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: In 2025, Blake Harbour worked as a senior staff engineer at ExampleCode.

pairs.rationale: The passage is an exact match for the claim about the open-source library.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi maintains the ExampleCode streaming connector used by several internal pipelines.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi maintains the ExampleCode streaming connector used by several internal pipelines.

pairs.rationale: The conference talk description states verbatim what the claim asserts.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone presented a talk on distributed tracing at the 2023 Vellum Robotics engineering summit.
pairs.passage: Avery Stone presented a talk on distributed tracing at the 2023 Vellum Robotics engineering summit.

pairs.rationale: The article title and byline match the claim exactly.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour published an article titled "Idempotent Delivery in Practice" in 2022.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour published an article titled "Idempotent Delivery in Practice" in 2022.

pairs.rationale: The passage restates the mentorship claim word for word.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi mentored five junior engineers during her tenure at Vellum Robotics.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi mentored five junior engineers during her tenure at Vellum Robotics.

pairs.rationale: The passage uses different wording for the same assertion, so the citation supports the claim in substance.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone led the reliability group at Vellum Robotics.
pairs.passage: At Vellum Robotics, Avery Stone spearheaded the reliability group, setting its roadmap and hiring plan.

pairs.rationale: "Designed and shipped" is a paraphrase of "built", so the claim is supported.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour built the notification service that ExampleCode runs in production today.
pairs.passage: While at ExampleCode, Blake Harbour designed and shipped the notification service that the company runs in production today.

pairs.rationale: "Chief architect" is a paraphrase of "technical lead", so the citation supports the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi was the technical lead for the billing rewrite at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: The ExampleCode billing rewrite succeeded largely because Priya Nandi served as its chief architect.

pairs.rationale: "Runs the ML platform group" is a paraphrase of "manages the machine learning platform team".
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone manages the machine learning platform team at Vellum Robotics.
pairs.passage: Vellum Robotics credits Avery Stone with running its ML platform group day to day.

pairs.rationale: "Keynote address" is a paraphrase of "opening talk", so the passage supports the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour delivered the opening talk at the ExampleCode developer conference in 2024.
pairs.passage: The 2024 ExampleCode developer conference opened with a keynote address given by Blake Harbour.

pairs.rationale: "Wrote the deployment tooling" is a paraphrase of "authored the deployment tools".
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi authored the deployment tools adopted across ExampleCode's infrastructure org.
pairs.passage: Engineers across ExampleCode's infrastructure org deploy with tooling that Priya Nandi wrote.

pairs.rationale: The Spanish-language passage asserts the same fact as the English claim, so the citation supports it across languages.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone led the search infrastructure team at Vellum Robotics in 2024.
pairs.passage: En 2024, Avery Stone dirigió el equipo de infraestructura de búsqueda en Vellum Robotics.

pairs.rationale: The French-language profile entry states the same role and employer as the English claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi works as a principal engineer at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi occupe le poste d'ingénieure principale chez ExampleCode.

pairs.rationale: A mention of a project does not establish that the person built it, so the passage cannot confirm the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone built the Vellum Robotics feature-flag service.
pairs.passage: The Vellum Robotics feature-flag service came up repeatedly during the design review Avery Stone attended.

pairs.rationale: Being quoted in connection with a system is not evidence of having built it.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour built ExampleCode's data lake ingestion pipeline.
pairs.passage: "The ingestion pipeline is our biggest source of surprises," Blake Harbour said in an interview about ExampleCode's data platform.

pairs.rationale: The passage places the person near the library without saying they authored it.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi created the ExampleCode retry library.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi's team discusses the retry library frequently in planning documents archived by ExampleCode.

pairs.rationale: Appearing on a podcast that discusses a tool does not establish the person wrote the tool.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone wrote the Vellum Robotics incident-response bot.
pairs.passage: On the Vellum Robotics engineering podcast, Avery Stone fielded questions about how the incident-response bot changed on-call work.

pairs.rationale: A thank-you acknowledgement is not attribution of authorship.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour built the ExampleCode schema registry.
pairs.passage: The ExampleCode schema registry README thanks Blake Harbour for feedback on its compatibility rules.

pairs.rationale: Reviewing a paper does not mean the reviewer built the system the paper describes.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi built the observability platform described in that paper.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi is listed among the reviewers of a paper describing an observability platform used at scale.

pairs.rationale: Working at the company during its founding era is not the same as founding it.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone co-founded Vellum Robotics.
pairs.passage: Avery Stone joined Vellum Robotics in its first year as one of the earliest engineers on the payroll.

pairs.rationale: Teaching at the school is employment, not founding it.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour founded the ExampleCode engineering academy.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour teaches the distributed systems course at the ExampleCode engineering academy.

pairs.rationale: Being an early employee does not establish founder status.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi founded the Vellum Robotics platform division.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi was among the first hires onto Vellum Robotics' newly created platform division.

pairs.rationale: Organizing a meetup chapter is affiliation, not founding the conference the claim names.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour founded the ExampleCode developer conference.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour organizes the local meetup chapter that feeds talks into the ExampleCode developer conference.

pairs.rationale: The passage explicitly states the person founded the organization named in the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi founded the streaming-analytics startup called Delta Mill.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi founded Delta Mill, a streaming-analytics startup, in 2021 and served as its first CEO.

pairs.rationale: A past-tense passage cannot establish the person's current role, so the claim is not supported.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone currently works as a staff engineer at Vellum Robotics.
pairs.passage: Avery Stone worked as a staff engineer at Vellum Robotics from 2019 to 2023.

pairs.rationale: The passage describes a former position, which cannot confirm a present-tense claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour is the director of infrastructure at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour served as director of infrastructure at ExampleCode until stepping down in 2022.

pairs.rationale: A past award does not establish a current title.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi currently holds the title of distinguished engineer at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: In 2021, Priya Nandi received ExampleCode's engineer of the year award while holding a senior title.

pairs.rationale: "Used to run" denotes a past responsibility only, so it cannot support the current-role claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone runs the Vellum Robotics build infrastructure today.
pairs.passage: Back in 2020, Avery Stone used to run the Vellum Robotics build infrastructure before it moved to a dedicated team.

pairs.rationale: The passage's "was" construction marks the role as historical, not current.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour is ExampleCode's technical spokesperson.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour was the public face of ExampleCode's developer relations efforts during its growth years.

pairs.rationale: A previously held title cannot establish the current title claimed.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi is presently a VP of engineering.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi once held the title of VP of engineering at a mid-sized logistics company.

pairs.rationale: The passage explicitly denies what the claim asserts, so the citation contradicts the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone led the Vellum Robotics mobile team.
pairs.passage: Contrary to some profiles, Avery Stone never led the Vellum Robotics mobile team.

pairs.rationale: The passage directly states the person did not work at the company named in the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour worked as an engineer at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour has confirmed that he never worked at ExampleCode in any capacity.

pairs.rationale: The source explicitly refutes the attribution of the open-source project to the person.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi created the ExampleCode migration framework.
pairs.passage: The ExampleCode migration framework was created by another team; Priya Nandi is not its creator.

pairs.rationale: The passage states the person did not found the organization the claim says they founded.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone founded the Delta Mill analytics startup.
pairs.passage: Delta Mill's official history lists different founders and notes that Avery Stone was not among them.

pairs.rationale: The source flatly denies the claimed degree.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour holds a PhD in computer science.
pairs.passage: Blake Harbour has stated publicly that he does not hold a PhD in computer science or any other field.

pairs.rationale: The passage is a name-and-title fragment with no predicate establishing employment, so it cannot support the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone currently works at Vellum Robotics as a platform engineer.
pairs.passage: Avery Stone — Platform Engineer. (see slides)

pairs.rationale: A bare citation-style listing without a verb carries no assertion that can support the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour led the ExampleCode search team in 2023.
pairs.passage: "Blake Harbour, ExampleCode Search" — conference attendee listing, 2023.

pairs.rationale: A photo caption fragment with no predicate cannot establish the claimed role.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi manages the Vellum Robotics data platform team.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi, Vellum Robotics data platform. [photo]

pairs.rationale: The passage is a truncated heading with no assertion, so it cannot support the employment claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone joined ExampleCode as a senior engineer in 2024.
pairs.passage: Related: Avery Stone, ExampleCode (2024)

pairs.rationale: The passage could plausibly describe two different appearances of the same content, so it cannot uniquely confirm the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone delivered two distinct talks at the 2024 ExampleCode conference.
pairs.passage: The 2024 ExampleCode conference schedule lists a talk by Avery Stone; the same title appears again later in the printed program.

pairs.rationale: Because the identical passage could occur twice in the corpus, a single occurrence cannot establish the claimed uniqueness.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour is the only ExampleCode engineer to have published that blog post.
pairs.passage: ExampleCode's blog contains a post by Blake Harbour; an identical byline line appears elsewhere in the archive.

pairs.rationale: An assertion on the person's own profile is self-reported and not independently established, so it cannot support the claim on its own.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone led a 40-person organization at Vellum Robotics.
pairs.passage: On his own profile page, Avery Stone writes: "I led a 40-person organization at Vellum Robotics."

pairs.rationale: A self-authored bio assertion is not independent evidence for the claimed credential.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi holds a master's degree from a top-ten engineering school.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi's self-written bio states that she holds a master's degree from a top-ten engineering school.

pairs.rationale: A self-reported patent count has not been independently verified and cannot support the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour is named on six granted patents.
pairs.passage: In his personal website's about section, Blake Harbour says he is named on six granted patents.

pairs.rationale: A first-person testimonial on the person's own page is self-report, not third-party confirmation.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone increased Vellum Robotics' deployment frequency by ten times.
pairs.passage: Avery Stone's own newsletter reads: "Under my leadership, Vellum Robotics increased deployment frequency tenfold."

pairs.rationale: The claim rests solely on the person's own account of the project's impact.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi's open-source library has over ten thousand weekly downloads.
pairs.passage: Priya Nandi states in her project README: "This library has over ten thousand weekly downloads."

pairs.rationale: The archived passage is undated, so it cannot establish that the role holds for the current claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone currently serves as Vellum Robotics' engineering manager for search.
pairs.passage: An archived copy of a team page lists Avery Stone as engineering manager for search at Vellum Robotics. (capture undated)

pairs.rationale: Without a capture date, the archived bio cannot establish present employment at the company.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour is presently employed at ExampleCode.
pairs.passage: A wayback snapshot shows a bio reading "Blake Harbour, engineer at ExampleCode." (no capture timestamp recorded)

pairs.rationale: The undated archive cannot establish that the title is current for the present-tense claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi currently holds the title of principal engineer.
pairs.passage: An archived résumé page shows Priya Nandi with the title principal engineer. (page undated)

pairs.rationale: The record lists the degree, institution, and date explicitly, which is sufficient to support the credential claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Avery Stone earned a bachelor's degree in computer science from Harborview University in 2015.
pairs.passage: Credential record: Degree — B.S. Computer Science; Institution — Harborview University; Date — May 2015.

pairs.rationale: Explicit credential, institution, and date lines fully support the master's degree claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi holds a master's degree in software engineering from Delta Institute, awarded in 2018.
pairs.passage: Credential record: Degree — M.S. Software Engineering; Institution — Delta Institute; Date — June 2018.

pairs.rationale: The certification, issuer, and year are each stated explicitly, supporting the claim.
pairs.claimStatement: Blake Harbour obtained a cloud architecture certification from the Open Systems Board in 2022.
pairs.passage: Credential record: Certification — Cloud Architecture Professional; Issuer — Open Systems Board; Date — March 2022.

pairs.rationale: The doctorate, institution, and completion year are explicitly listed, so the claim is supported.
pairs.claimStatement: Priya Nandi completed a PhD in distributed systems at Harborview University in 2021.
pairs.passage: Credential record: Degree — PhD, Distributed Systems; Institution — Harborview University; Date — August 2021.

pairs.rationale: The passage describes the program itself, not the person's participation, so it cannot establish the credential was earned.
